---
title: Forecasting Risk
output: pdf_document
---

What is forecasting risk? In general, would the degree of forecasting risk be
greater for a new product or a cost-cutting proposal? Why?

> When making an estimate of revenues and costs of a project, the variables
> need to be identified. Once identified, the values of these variables need to
> be guestimated in order to develop models for the revenues and costs of the
> project. forecasting risk is the risk of an error in these forecasting
> values. A change in a single forecast can greatly alter the NPV estimate of
> the project.
>
> Sensitivity analysis can be used to identify if the NPV value of the project
> can be trusted. Sensitivity analysis consists of identifying a pessimistic,
> base, and optimistic values for each of the variables and vary the values of
> the variables to calculate the NPV. If the dispersion of the NPV values is
> not wide, then it may be okay to trust the NPV value.
